title: Publish REVIEW_HANDLERS on the @moe/daemon root
description:
Objective: publish the committed review command surface on the @moe/daemon package root so the Foundation canary and any external consumer can drive it. Created by governor-f70d1157 on 2026-08-09 at explicit human direction, after the ask was routed to three architects who each auto-claimed from the PLANNING queue instead. A governor created this task; an ARCHITECT must still plan it — do not treat the description below as a plan.

WHY THIS EXISTS. task-9011e3b32c ("Persist the review flow: finding lineage, invalidation and carry-forward") landed the full review command surface and was QA-approved DONE at 11:46Z. apps/daemon/src/review/ is tracked: 18 files including .js runtime bridges for every runtime module (review-contracts.js, review-ledger.js, review-read-model.js, review-services.js, review-delta.js, review-acceptance.js). But the daemon root never gained the export, because index.ts was outside that task's owned paths. Its worker disclosed the omission in their step notes rather than reaching into a foreign path — that was correct behaviour under epic rail 3, and THIS TASK IS NOT A DEFECT FIX. Write it up as a follow-on.

MEASURED ON DISK by governor-f70d1157 at 11:47Z, HEAD 1ce0059:
- `grep -c REVIEW_HANDLERS apps/daemon/src/index.ts` returns 0.
- `apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts:131` reads `expect(EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length).toBe(31)`.
- REVIEW_HANDLERS is defined at apps/daemon/src/review/review-services.ts:159 as a frozen HandlerTable with four handlers: "escalation.decide", "integration.accept_output", "qualification.replan", "review.submit". The pipeline entry point is runReviewCommand in the same file. Read these modules before naming a single symbol; do not copy names from this description without verifying each on disk.

THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF ONE PATTERN, and the three prior fixes are the template: task-8ee125d0 for @moe/scheduler (commit 239aa4f), task-53680e91 for @moe/runner, and task-6054520bc for the daemon's first publication. USE task-6054520bc AS THE LITERAL TEMPLATE — it is DONE, it is four steps, and it published the existing 31-symbol surface this task extends by one.

THIS IS THE CANARY'S LAST BLOCKER. task-97554aa4 (Foundation self-host canary, CRITICAL) is BLOCKED and its other three block claims are already false on disk: goal.close is in GOAL_HANDLERS (goal-services.ts:113, exported at index.ts:40); approval.decide composes activateInitialGraph as a single durable commit (planning-services.ts:175); integration.accept_output exists in REVIEW_HANDLERS. Both gating tasks are DONE — task-671578e5c cleared QA at 11:33Z, task-9011e3b32c at 11:46Z. Global rail Clause 1 is why the canary is still held: exporting symbols into a directory is not composition, and a canary that cannot reach review commands through production authority would re-block. governor-f70d1157 unblocks task-97554aa4 once this lands and the export is verified reachable.

NOT in scope: changing ANY behaviour in any daemon or review module; exporting test-only modules (review-test-fixtures.ts is fixtures — do NOT export it); touching packages/**; any package.json or lockfile edit; adding .js bridges (they already exist under apps/daemon/src/review/).

Hard dependencies: none. Every surface named above is committed at HEAD 1ce0059.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/index.ts and apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts.
NOTE ON THE SECOND OWNED PATH: index-surface.test.ts is task-6054520bc's owned file. Updating its EXPECTED_EXPORTS list and cardinality guard is REQUIRED CO-CHANGE, not scope creep — both qa-58b24ffb and qa-b2df68b9 have stated on the record that they will not reject on it, and will reject if index.ts gains the export while that test is left red.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck, PLUS a plain-Node root import probe (see task rails).

Expected size: 4-6 steps. If the plan comes out materially larger, something has been misread — report it rather than padding.
definitionOfDone: apps/daemon/src/index.ts exports REVIEW_HANDLERS from ./review/review-services.js, plus the review type closure a consumer needs to name every parameter and discriminate every union arm of the review command path (including ReviewOutcome and the request/result types runReviewCommand consumes and returns), using curated named exports with .js specifiers and the `type` modifier, in the same grouped style the file already uses. No export-star.

apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts asserts REVIEW_HANDLERS is present with the expected typeof, via the package ROOT specifier @moe/daemon and never a relative or deep path, so a dropped export fails by name rather than by a count.

The EXPECTED_EXPORTS list in index-surface.test.ts gains the literal name REVIEW_HANDLERS AND the cardinality guard at line 131 moves from 31 to 32. Both changes are required together: a bare number bump to 32 with no name added defeats the guard and is an explicit rejection condition already agreed by both QA agents.

Reachability is proved by a PLAIN-NODE root import probe, not by vitest, and the probe output is recorded verbatim in the completion evidence. Vitest resolves a NodeNext ".js" specifier back to ".ts" and is structurally blind to a missing bridge — task-6054520bc sat at 46/46 green while plain Node died ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on exactly this surface. The probe must show REVIEW_HANDLERS present as an object with its four handler keys.
No test-only module reaches the runtime surface — review-test-fixtures.ts in particular stays internal — asserted by the set-equality list, not by inspection.

Zero behaviour change: git diff shows apps/daemon/src/index.ts as the only modified non-test file, no .js bridge is added, no review or daemon service module is edited, and the daemon suite's test count is greater than or equal to the pre-task count, stated as an explicit before/after number.

pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck all exit 0. Foreign red is attributed by path per global rail 3 and disclosed verbatim, never hidden and never fabricated green.
taskRails: Re-export only. This task changes what is REACHABLE, never what any function DOES. No .ts file other than index.ts and index-surface.test.ts may be edited. If a symbol seems to need a signature change to be exportable, report_blocked rather than editing a review or daemon service module.

Read apps/daemon/src/review/review-services.ts and review-ledger.ts before naming a symbol; do not guess export names and do not copy them from this description without verifying each one on disk (skill: explore-before-assume).
Never export a test-only module. review-test-fixtures.ts stays internal; exporting fixtures puts test code on the runtime surface.
Prefer curated named exports over a blanket `export *`, so the published seam stays a reviewed decision rather than whatever the module happens to export next week.

PROVE IT WITH PLAIN NODE, NOT VITEST. A green vitest suite is not evidence for a task whose whole objective is that an external consumer can import the surface. Run the root import from apps/daemon with plain Node and record the output. Note: shell cwd persists between tool calls — after cd apps/daemon, later repo-relative git pathspecs silently match nothing, which is indistinguishable from a clean tree.
Assert against the production surface obtained through the @moe/daemon root import, never against a locally re-declared type or a fixture copy.

Keep the entry point focused: target <=250 lines, split before 400. index.ts was 222 lines after task-6054520bc, so budget accordingly; if the added exports push it past 250, extract a per-area re-export module that index.ts re-exports rather than letting the entry point sprawl.

Commit by explicit pathspec only — git commit -- apps/daemon/src/index.ts apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts — never a bare git commit or git add -A. Several agents share this working directory. Verify with git show --stat afterwards. If a foreign completion hook has already swept your files into another task's commit, do NOT amend it and do NOT create an empty commit: report the base-ref diff QA should review instead.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Mirror the already-approved daemon root-publication pattern: add one package-root runtime symbol plus its type-only closure. Do not export runReviewCommand, decodeReviewRequestBytes, review constants, or fixtures: the task mechanically fixes the runtime export-set cardinality at 32, so REVIEW_HANDLERS is the sole new runtime export. Do not create an area barrel because ownership is limited to the two named files; keep the curated declarations compact enough for index.ts to remain at or below 250 physical lines, otherwise report blocked rather than widening scope.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: apps/daemon/src/index.ts is currently 222 lines and uses explicit .js re-exports. Existing bootstrap exports already occupy the names CommandHandler, HandlerContext, and HandlerTable, so the review equivalents must be exposed as ReviewCommandHandler, ReviewHandlerContext, and ReviewHandlerTable aliases. REVIEW_HANDLERS is a frozen object in review/review-services.ts with exactly escalation.decide, integration.accept_output, qualification.replan, and review.submit. index-surface.test.ts imports through @moe/daemon and currently pins 31 runtime exports; adding type-only exports will not alter that set.
planningNotes.risks: Vitest can hide package-root/runtime loader mistakes, so retain the required plain-Node probe from apps/daemon. A mere typeof assertion would accept the wrong handler table; pin the exact four-key set through the production package root. Exact export-set equality must also catch accidental fixture or extra runtime exports. Keep the test red for the intended missing root symbol before production edits, preserve daemon test-count baseline, and never change review implementation modules or signatures.
